reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes BitConnect lending as an accessible, deposit-like way for ordinary people to earn almost 1% interest per day, while directing viewers toward participation through a BitConnect referral link. Although the speaker briefly acknowledges risk, he calls BitConnect one of his favorites, describes having approximately $19,000 there, and ends by saying it is a great time to get in, which makes the overall communication an endorsement rather than a warning.

opening.argument: Judge the return claim alongside the speaker's qualification of it. He says the rate sounds unusually high and immediately warns that it carries risk. Earlier, he tells newcomers that cryptocurrency is not guaranteed and urges them not to go in blind. He also describes prices as volatile and offers market commentary about buying and selling. That combination supports reading this as candid, if enthusiastic, investment commentary rather than a promise that viewers will earn a dependable return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited daily figure is presented as what the speaker says he is getting, not as a guaranteed rate for every viewer. The closing invitation also follows his broader discussion of cryptocurrency; its few words do not specify BitConnect. The referral link establishes an incentive, but it does not erase his explicit warning about the unusually high rate. Read the endorsement with that warning, not in isolation.

opening.argument: The speaker introduces this as a general starting point for people new to cryptocurrency, with more detailed subjects deferred to later videos. Much of the instruction concerns operational questions: where to purchase cryptocurrency, how to transfer it to a wallet, and why offline storage matters. He also walks through converting cryptocurrency to a bank payment. BitConnect appears within a survey of ways people use cryptocurrency, so the judge should assess the video as a broad beginner tutorial rather than treating that one segment as its entire purpose.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening isolates the BitConnect passage from an introduction that also explains exchanges, storage and other ways of participating. Calling a platform a favorite and describing an experience there can be part of teaching newcomers what the speaker has tried. The final 'Great time to get in' follows a Bitcoin price projection, so it is not clearly an instruction to enter BitConnect specifically.

The speaker tells a layperson how to put Bitcoin into BitConnect, buy its coin and lend, then presents his claimed daily interest and calls it a favorite platform. A BitConnect referral link gives viewers a route to act on that pitch. Other instructional material does not neutralize those specific promotional claims.

opening.argument: A referral link identifies a commercial relationship, but the supplied material does not by itself establish that the linked service fails to deliver or that the speaker receives money from viewers' deposits. The speaker discusses multiple services for buying, exchanging and spending cryptocurrency, alongside hardware used for storage. He describes his BitConnect activity as his own experience and expressly acknowledges risk. The judge can recognize ordinary service promotion and personal experience without assuming that an external platform is safe or that a deceptive mechanism has been demonstrated.
